posts.title: RTX 5070 vs RTX 5070 Ti: Is the Ti Worth It in 2027?
posts.excerpt: The RTX 5070 Ti is 24% faster and has 16GB of VRAM instead of 12GB, for $200 more at launch. Which one makes sense for 2027 games.
posts.content:
The RTX 5070 Ti is 24% faster than the RTX 5070 on our performance index, and it has 16GB of video memory where the 5070 has 12GB. The Ti launched at $749, which is $200 above the 5070's $549.

Both cards come from the same RTX 50 generation with the same feature set, so the choice comes down to three things: how much the extra speed is worth to you, whether 12GB will be enough for the games you plan to play, and how long you intend to keep the card.

RTX 5070 vs RTX 5070 Ti: the specs side by side

RTX 5070RTX 5070 Ti
Performance index6378
Relative speed100%124%
Video memory12GB16GB
Board power250W300W
Launch price (MSRP)$549$749
Index points per $10011.510.4
Index points per 100W25.226.0
Released20252025
Upscaling supportDLSS, FSRDLSS, FSR
Recommended specs met, 2024+ games19 of 1919 of 19
Recommended specs met, upcoming games15 of 1616 of 16

"Recommended specs met" counts the games whose recommended graphics card each GPU matches or beats. It covers the 19 games from 2024 onward in our catalogue that name a recommended card, and the 16 unreleased games whose publishers have posted one.

Speed: how big is the gap?

A 24% lead on the index is roughly the difference between a game holding a steady frame rate and dipping below it at the same settings. The more useful test is what each card clears. Among 19 recent games that name a recommended card, the RTX 5070 meets 19 and the Ti meets 19. For unreleased games the count is 15 against 16 out of 16.

Only the Ti clears the recommended card for Lords of the Fallen II.

12GB or 16GB of VRAM?

This is the Ti's clearest advantage. Lords of the Fallen II already asks for more than 12GB at the recommended tier, by naming a card with more memory or by stating the figure outright. Recommended specs are usually written with 1080p or 1440p in mind, though. Higher resolutions, ultra textures and path tracing fill memory well beyond what a requirement table suggests, and a card cannot be upgraded later. See how much VRAM 2027 games actually ask for.

Value and power

At launch prices, the RTX 5070 delivers 11.5 index points per $100 and the Ti delivers 10.4, so the cheaper card gives more performance for each dollar. The Ti's board power is 50W higher (300W against 250W). Check your power supply with the PSU calculator before you switch.

Verdict

  • Buy the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 if price per frame matters most, since it returns more performance per dollar, and you play at 1080p or 1440p without maxed-out texture packs.
  • Buy the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti if you want to keep the card for years. The 16GB buffer and the 24% extra speed are the two things that age best.

posts.title: RTX 5080 vs RTX 5090: How Much Faster Is the 5090?
posts.excerpt: The RTX 5090 is 44% faster than the RTX 5080 with twice the VRAM, but it costs $1000 more and draws 215W extra. What that buys you.
posts.content:
The RTX 5090 is 44% faster than the RTX 5080 on our performance index and doubles its video memory, from 16GB to 32GB. It also doubles the price: $1999 at launch against $999.

The spec sheet makes the 5090 look like the obvious winner. The real question is whether any game you will play in 2027 needs it, and here the published requirements give a clear answer.

"Recommended specs met" counts the games whose recommended graphics card each GPU matches or beats. It covers the 19 games from 2024 onward in our catalogue that name a recommended card, and the 16 unreleased games whose publishers have posted one.

Does any game need an RTX 5090?

Not yet. The RTX 5080 already meets the recommended graphics card of all 16 unreleased games that have posted one, and 19 of the 19 recent games that name a recommended card. Every extra frame the 5090 delivers goes beyond what publishers ask for. That is why it matters most for 4K at high refresh rates, heavy path tracing and creative work that fills 32GB of memory.

What the extra $1000 buys

Measured per dollar, the RTX 5080 returns 8.9 index points per $100 and the 5090 returns 6.4. The step up is 44% more performance for 100% more money, which is typical of flagship pricing.

Power and heat

The 5090 is rated at 575W of board power, 215W more than the 5080's 360W. That often means a new power supply, and it always means more heat in the case. Run your parts through the PSU calculator before you buy.

Verdict

  • Buy the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 for gaming. It meets every published recommended spec for upcoming games and delivers more performance per dollar.
  • Buy the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 if you play at 4K with path tracing, want the most headroom money can buy, or need 32GB of memory for work as well as play.

posts.title: RTX 4090 vs RTX 5090: Is Upgrading Worth It?
posts.excerpt: The RTX 5090 is 28% faster than the RTX 4090 and adds 8GB of VRAM. Whether a 4090 owner gains anything in 2027 games.
posts.content:
The RTX 5090 is 28% faster than the RTX 4090 on our performance index and has 32GB of video memory against 24GB. Their launch prices were $1999 and $1599.

Most people asking this question already own a 4090 and want to know whether the newer card is worth the switch. For most games the answer is no.

"Recommended specs met" counts the games whose recommended graphics card each GPU matches or beats. It covers the 19 games from 2024 onward in our catalogue that name a recommended card, and the 16 unreleased games whose publishers have posted one.

The RTX 4090 still clears everything

The RTX 4090 meets the recommended graphics card of all 16 unreleased games whose publishers have posted one, and 19 of the 19 recent games that name a recommended card. No published requirement for 2027 comes close to it. An upgrade buys headroom above what games ask for, not the ability to run them.

What is new on the RTX 5090

Beyond the 28% speed gain and the extra memory, the 5090 belongs to the RTX 50 generation. That matters for one feature: DLSS 4's Multi Frame Generation, which inserts several generated frames per rendered frame, runs only on RTX 50-series cards. The 4090 keeps DLSS upscaling and single frame generation. If a high-refresh 4K monitor is the goal, that feature is the strongest argument for the switch.

Power

The 5090 is rated at 575W, 125W above the 4090's 450W. A power supply that was comfortable for a 4090 may be marginal for a 5090, so check with the PSU calculator.

Verdict

  • Keep the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 if you play at 1440p or 4K at ordinary refresh rates. Nothing announced for 2027 asks for more.
  • Upgrade to the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 if you want Multi Frame Generation for a very high-refresh 4K display, or need 32GB of memory for AI or 3D work.

posts.title: RX 9070 XT vs RTX 5070 Ti: Which to Buy in 2027?
posts.excerpt: The RX 9070 XT and RTX 5070 Ti are within a few percent on our index, both with 16GB, but launched $150 apart. How to choose.
posts.content:
On raw performance the RX 9070 XT and the RTX 5070 Ti are practically tied: 77 against 78 on our index, a 1% gap. Both have 16GB of video memory. The AMD card launched at $599, which was $150 less than NVIDIA's $749.

When two cards are this close, the choice comes down to price, upscaling technology and power draw rather than frame rates.

Game requirements: a draw

Among 19 recent games that name a recommended card, the RX 9070 XT meets 19 and the RTX 5070 Ti meets 19. For unreleased games with published specs, the count is 16 against 16 out of 16. With the same 16GB buffer, neither card has a memory advantage to grow into.

Price per frame

At launch prices, the RX 9070 XT gives 12.9 index points per $100 and the RTX 5070 Ti gives 10.4. The AMD card delivers 23% more performance for each dollar, which is the single biggest difference between them.

DLSS or FSR

The RTX 5070 Ti supports NVIDIA's DLSS, which more games have adopted, including Multi Frame Generation on RTX 50 cards. The RX 9070 XT uses AMD's FSR. FSR 4, AMD's machine-learning upscaler, is limited to Radeon RX 9000 cards like this one, and game support is still catching up with DLSS. If a game you care about only offers DLSS, that settles it. Compare what each card gets on the DLSS vs FSR page.

Power

Board power is close: 304W for the RX 9070 XT and 300W for the RTX 5070 Ti. Either card fits the same power supply.

Verdict

  • Buy the AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT if price decides. It matches the Ti in the games that matter for less money.
  • Buy the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti if you want DLSS and Multi Frame Generation, or the games you play favour NVIDIA's feature set.

posts.excerpt: Both launched at $299 with 8GB of VRAM, but the RTX 5060 is 17% faster on our index. What changed, and whether the 8GB limit matters in 2027.
posts.content:
The RTX 5060 is 17% faster than the RTX 4060 on our performance index, and it launched at the same $299. Both cards have 8GB of video memory, and the newer card is rated 30W higher (145W against 115W).

If you are buying new, the 5060 is the better card at that price. If you already own a 4060, the gap is too small to justify replacing it.

What each card clears

Among 19 recent games that name a recommended card, the RTX 4060 meets 14 and the RTX 5060 meets 16. For unreleased games with published specs, it is 7 against 10 of 16. Only the 5060 clears the recommended card for SAW: Genesis, Gears of War: E-Day and The Talos Principle 3.

The 8GB question

Speed is not what limits these cards; memory is. posts.title: Is 8GB of VRAM Enough for Gaming in 2027?
posts.excerpt: 8GB meets the recommended spec of 11 of 16 upcoming PC games that state one. Which games need more, and when 8GB starts to hold you back.
posts.content:
8GB of VRAM is still enough to meet the recommended requirements of 11 of the 16 upcoming PC games whose publishers have named a card or a memory figure. The 5 that ask for more (31%) are the ones to watch: Fable, Outward 2, Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, The Talos Principle 3 and Lords of the Fallen II. No upcoming game needs more than 8GB to meet its minimum spec.

So the short answer is yes for most games at 1080p, and "only with compromises" for the heaviest new releases at higher resolutions. The rest of this page shows where that line sits, game by game.

What upcoming games ask for

For each game, this is the larger of two figures: the memory on the recommended card the publisher named, or a VRAM amount the publisher wrote down.

Recommended VRAMGamesWhich
16GB1Lords of the Fallen II
12GB3Fable, Outward 2, The Talos Principle 3
10GB1Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis
8GB10SPINE - This is Gun Fu, HUMANKIND 2, SAW: Genesis, Chrono Odyssey, PVKK: Planetenverteidigungskanonenkommandant, Gears of War: E-Day, Sagas of Lumin, Sea of Remnants, Phantom Blade Zero, Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance
2GB1Pony Island 2: Panda Circus

What recent released games ask for

Of the 19 games from 2024 onward in our catalogue that name a recommended card with a known memory size, 2 (11%) point to more than 8GB. Across the whole catalogue it is 9 of 216. Requirement tables lag behind what games actually use: a publisher writes a recommended spec for 1080p or 1440p at high settings, not for 4K with the highest texture pack.

When 8GB runs out

  • Resolution. 1440p and 4K use far more memory than 1080p for the same game.
  • Texture quality. The top texture setting is usually the biggest single consumer of VRAM, and dropping it one step is often enough to fit in 8GB.
  • Ray tracing and frame generation. Both add memory overhead on top of the base game.

When a game runs out of video memory, the result is stutter and blurry, late-loading textures rather than a lower average frame rate. That makes the problem easy to miss in a benchmark chart and hard to ignore in play.

Still buying an 8GB card?

New 8GB cards are still on sale. The fastest recent ones in our index are NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 8GB, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5050. They are fine for 1080p. If you plan to keep a card through 2027 and beyond, or play at 1440p, 12GB is the safer floor. Compare the options on the GPU tier list, or see how the RTX 5060 and RTX 4060 and the RTX 5070 and 5070 Ti compare.

You do not need that much to play most of them. The NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 ($299) already meets 18 of 19 minimum specs and 10 of 16 recommended ones.

One game pulls the bar for minimums up on its own: SAW: Genesis names the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 as its minimum. Leave it out and the Intel Arc B580 ($249) meets every other minimum. How to read "specs met"

A card meets a requirement when it scores at least as high as the card the publisher named on our performance index and has any VRAM amount the publisher stated. posts.title: 16GB vs 32GB RAM for Gaming in 2027
posts.excerpt: 16GB meets the recommended RAM of 14 of 16 upcoming PC games that state it. Which games want 32GB, and when the upgrade is worth it.
posts.content:
16GB of RAM is still enough for gaming: it meets the recommended memory of 14 of the 16 upcoming PC games that state one. The exceptions are Chrono Odyssey and Sea of Remnants, which recommend 32GB. 9 games already treat 16GB as the bare minimum, so 8GB is no longer a realistic gaming configuration.

Whether 32GB is worth buying depends less on today's requirement tables than on what else runs while you play, and on how long the PC has to last.

Upcoming games: recommended RAM

Recommended RAMGamesWhich
32GB2Chrono Odyssey, Sea of Remnants
16GB12SPINE - This is Gun Fu, Fable, Outward 2, SAW: Genesis, PVKK: Planetenverteidigungskanonenkommandant, Gears of War: E-Day, Sagas of Lumin, Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, The Talos Principle 3, Phantom Blade Zero, Lords of the Fallen II, Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance
12GB1HUMANKIND 2
8GB1Pony Island 2: Panda Circus

Recent released games

Of the 20 games from 2024 onward in our catalogue that state a recommended amount, 14 ask for exactly 16GB and 1 asks for 32GB or more. The move to 32GB is happening, but slowly. Publishers raise the minimum before they raise the recommended figure.

When 32GB makes a difference

  • Background apps. A browser, Discord and a streaming or recording tool can take several gigabytes between them. That is memory the game cannot use.
  • Large open worlds and simulations. Strategy, city-builder and flight-sim games tend to use more memory than their requirement tables suggest, especially late in a save.
  • Keeping the PC for years. Memory requirements only go up, and adding a second pair of sticks later is not always possible at the same speed.

Verdict

  • 16GB if you mainly game, keep background apps light and build on a tight budget. It covers almost every published 2027 requirement.
  • 32GB for a new build meant to last, or if you stream, record or keep a lot open while playing. It is also required for Chrono Odyssey and Sea of Remnants at the recommended tier.

To see whether the rest of your PC keeps up, run it through the can my PC run it checker. For graphics memory rather than system memory, see is 8GB of VRAM enough.

How these numbers were worked out

Requirements are the publishers' own, read from each game's Steam store page (last checked 15 September 2026). Entries such as "TBD" or "Coming soon" count as not published, never as a spec. Graphics cards are compared on the relative performance index explained in our editorial standards, where a card "meets" a requirement when it scores at least as high as the card the publisher named and has any VRAM amount the publisher stated. This article is rebuilt whenever that data is refreshed.
